paper_title: Weak compactons of nonlinearly dispersive KdV and KP equations (Anco, 2024, Studies in Applied Mathematics)
core_reasoning_1:
\section*{Claim}
For the one-dimensional equation
\[
u_t+a(u^m)_x+b(u^n)_{xxx}=0
\]
and the traveling wave ansatz \(u(t,x)=U(\xi)\), \(\xi=x-ct\), the profile satisfies
\[
\left(-gU+aU^m+b(U^n)''\right)'=0,\qquad g=c.
\]
For the two-dimensional equation
\[
\left(u_t+a(u^m)_x+b(u^n)_{xxx}\right)_x+\sigma u_{yy}=0
\]
and the line traveling wave ansatz \(u(t,x,y)=U(\xi)\), \(\xi=x+\mu y-\nu t\), the profile satisfies
\[
\left(-gU+aU^m+b(U^n)''\right)''=0,\qquad g=\nu-\sigma\mu^2.
\]
If \(c=\nu/\sqrt{1+\mu^2}\) and \(\theta=\arctan(\mu)\), then
\[
g=c|\sec\theta|-\sigma\tan^2\theta.
\]

\section*{Premises}
\begin{align}
\text{(P1)}\quad &u_t+a(u^m)_x+b(u^n)_{xxx}=0,\qquad m,n>0,
\qquad a,b\ne0.\\
\text{(P2)}\quad &\left(u_t+a(u^m)_x+b(u^n)_{xxx}\right)_x+\sigma u_{yy}=0,
\qquad \sigma^2=1.\\
\text{(P3)}\quad &u(t,x)=U(\xi),\qquad \xi=x-ct.\\
\text{(P4)}\quad &u(t,x,y)=U(\xi),\qquad \xi=x+\mu y-\nu t.\\
\text{(P5)}\quad &\text{If }F(\xi)=F(U(\xi)),\text{ then }F_x=F',\quad F_t=-cF'
\quad\text{under (P3).}\\
\text{(P6)}\quad &\text{If }F(\xi)=F(U(\xi)),\text{ then }F_x=F',\quad F_t=-\nu F',
\quad F_y=\mu F'\quad\text{under (P4).}\\
\text{(P7)}\quad &c=\frac{\nu}{\sqrt{1+\mu^2}},\qquad \theta=\arctan(\mu),
\qquad \tan\theta=\mu,
\qquad |\sec\theta|=\sqrt{1+\mu^2}.
\end{align}

\section*{Derivation}
For the one-dimensional equation, substitute (P3) into (P1) and use (P5):
\begin{align}
0
&=u_t+a(u^m)_x+b(u^n)_{xxx} &&\text{by (P1)}\\
&=-cU'+a(U^m)'+b(U^n)''' &&\text{by (P3)--(P5)}\\
&=\left(-cU+aU^m+b(U^n)''\right)' &&\text{by linearity of }d/d\xi.
\end{align}
Define \(g:=c\). Then
\begin{align}
0
&=\left(-gU+aU^m+b(U^n)''\right)' &&\text{substitution of }g:=c.
\end{align}
For the two-dimensional equation, set
\[
Q:=u_t+a(u^m)_x+b(u^n)_{xxx}.
\]
Using (P4)--(P6),
\begin{align}
Q
&=-\nu U'+a(U^m)'+b(U^n)'''\\
&=\left(-\nu U+aU^m+b(U^n)''\right)'.
\end{align}
Substitute this expression for \(Q\) into (P2):
\begin{align}
0
&=Q_x+\sigma u_{yy} &&\text{by (P2)}\\
&=Q'+\sigma \mu^2U'' &&\text{by (P6)}\\
&=\left(-\nu U+aU^m+b(U^n)''\right)''+\sigma\mu^2U''\\
&=\left(-(\nu-\sigma\mu^2)U+aU^m+b(U^n)''\right)''.
\end{align}
Define \(g:=\nu-\sigma\mu^2\). Then
\begin{align}
0
&=\left(-gU+aU^m+b(U^n)''\right)''.
\end{align}
Finally, using (P7),
\begin{align}
g
&=\nu-\sigma\mu^2 &&\text{definition of }g\\
&=c\sqrt{1+\mu^2}-\sigma\mu^2 &&\text{because }c=\nu/\sqrt{1+\mu^2}\\
&=c|\sec\theta|-\sigma\tan^2\theta &&\text{by (P7)}.
\end{align}

\section*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{\begin{gathered}
\left(-gU+aU^m+b(U^n)''\right)'=0,\qquad g=c,\\
\left(-gU+aU^m+b(U^n)''\right)''=0,\qquad
 g=\nu-\sigma\mu^2=c|\sec\theta|-\sigma\tan^2\theta.
\end{gathered}}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_3:
\section*{Claim}
The weak form of the \(K(m,n)\) equation reduces, under \(u(t,x)=U(x-ct)\), to
\[
\iint_{\mathbb R^2}\left((-cU+aU^m)\psi_\xi+bU^n\psi_{\xi\xi\xi}\right)d\tau d\xi=0.
\]
The weak form of the \(KP(m,n)\) equation reduces, under \(u(t,x,y)=U(x+\mu y-\nu t)\), to
\[
\iiint_{\mathbb R^3}\left((-gU+aU^m)\psi_{\xi\xi}+bU^n\psi_{\xi\xi\xi\xi}\right)d\tau d\zeta d\xi=0,
\qquad g=\nu-\sigma\mu^2.
\]

\section*{Premises}
\begin{align}
\text{(P1)}\quad &\iint_{\mathbb R^2}\left(u\psi_t+a u^m\psi_x+b u^n\psi_{xxx}\right)dt dx=0
\quad\text{for all test functions }\psi(t,x).\\
\text{(P2)}\quad &\iiint_{\mathbb R^3}\left(u\psi_{tx}+\sigma u\psi_{yy}+a u^m\psi_{xx}+b u^n\psi_{xxxx}\right)dt dxdy=0
\quad\text{for all test functions }\psi(t,x,y).\\
\text{(P3)}\quad &u(t,x)=U(\xi),\qquad \xi=x-ct,
\qquad \tau=t,
\qquad dxdt=d\xi d\tau.\\
\text{(P4)}\quad &u(t,x,y)=U(\xi),\qquad \xi=x+\mu y-\nu t,
\qquad \tau=t,
\qquad \zeta=y,
\qquad dtdxdy=d\tau d\xi d\zeta.\\
\text{(P5)}\quad &\partial_t=\partial_\tau-c\partial_\xi,
\qquad \partial_x=\partial_\xi
\quad\text{under (P3).}\\
\text{(P6)}\quad &\partial_t=\partial_\tau-\nu\partial_\xi,
\qquad \partial_x=\partial_\xi,
\qquad \partial_y=\partial_\zeta+\mu\partial_\xi
\quad\text{under (P4).}\\
\text{(P7)}\quad &\int_{\mathbb R}U(\xi)\psi_\tau(\tau,\xi)\,d\tau=0,
\qquad
\int_{\mathbb R}U(\xi)\psi_{\tau\xi}(\tau,\xi,\zeta)\,d\tau=0
\quad\text{for compactly supported }\psi.\\
\text{(P8)}\quad &\int_{\mathbb R}U(\xi)\psi_{\zeta\zeta}(\tau,\xi,\zeta)\,d\zeta=0
\quad\text{for compactly supported }\psi.
\end{align}

\section*{Derivation}
For the \(K(m,n)\) equation, use (P3)--(P5) in (P1):
\begin{align}
0
&=\iint_{\mathbb R^2}\left(U(\psi_\tau-c\psi_\xi)+aU^m\psi_\xi+bU^n\psi_{\xi\xi\xi}\right)d\tau d\xi.
\end{align}
Separate the \(\psi_\tau\) term and apply (P7):
\begin{align}
0
&=\iint_{\mathbb R^2}U\psi_\tau\,d\tau d\xi
 +\iint_{\mathbb R^2}\left((-cU+aU^m)\psi_\xi+bU^n\psi_{\xi\xi\xi}\right)d\tau d\xi\\
&=\iint_{\mathbb R^2}\left((-cU+aU^m)\psi_\xi+bU^n\psi_{\xi\xi\xi}\right)d\tau d\xi.
\end{align}
For the \(KP(m,n)\) equation, use (P4)--(P6) in (P2):
\begin{align}
\psi_{tx}&=(\partial_\tau-\nu\partial_\xi)\partial_\xi\psi
=\psi_{\tau\xi}-\nu\psi_{\xi\xi},\\
\psi_{xx}&=\psi_{\xi\xi},
\qquad
\psi_{xxxx}=\psi_{\xi\xi\xi\xi},\\
\psi_{yy}&=(\partial_\zeta+\mu\partial_\xi)^2\psi
=\psi_{\zeta\zeta}+2\mu\psi_{\zeta\xi}+\mu^2\psi_{\xi\xi}.
\end{align}
The mixed \(\zeta\xi\) term integrates to zero because \(U\) is independent of \(\zeta\) and \(\psi\) is compactly supported:
\begin{align}
\int_{\mathbb R}U\psi_{\zeta\xi}\,d\zeta
&=\left[U\psi_\xi\right]_{\zeta=-\infty}^{\zeta=\infty}=0.
\end{align}
Therefore (P2), (P7), and (P8) give
\begin{align}
0
&=\iiint_{\mathbb R^3}\left(U(\psi_{\tau\xi}-\nu\psi_{\xi\xi})
+\sigma U(\psi_{\zeta\zeta}+2\mu\psi_{\zeta\xi}+\mu^2\psi_{\xi\xi})
+aU^m\psi_{\xi\xi}+bU^n\psi_{\xi\xi\xi\xi}\right)d\tau d\xi d\zeta\\
&=\iiint_{\mathbb R^3}\left((-(\nu-\sigma\mu^2)U+aU^m)\psi_{\xi\xi}
+bU^n\psi_{\xi\xi\xi\xi}\right)d\tau d\xi d\zeta.
\end{align}
Define \(g:=\nu-\sigma\mu^2\). Then
\begin{align}
0
&=\iiint_{\mathbb R^3}\left((-gU+aU^m)\psi_{\xi\xi}
+bU^n\psi_{\xi\xi\xi\xi}\right)d\tau d\xi d\zeta.
\end{align}

\section*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{\begin{gathered}
\iint_{\mathbb R^2}\left((-cU+aU^m)\psi_\xi+bU^n\psi_{\xi\xi\xi}\right)d\tau d\xi=0,\\
\iiint_{\mathbb R^3}\left((-gU+aU^m)\psi_{\xi\xi}+bU^n\psi_{\xi\xi\xi\xi}\right)d\tau d\zeta d\xi=0,
\quad g=\nu-\sigma\mu^2.
\end{gathered}}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_4:
\section*{Claim}
Let \(U_c(\xi)=U(\xi)H(L-|\xi|)\), where \(H\) is the Heaviside function. If \(U\) solves the traveling-wave ODE on \([-L,L]\), then the weak \(K(m,n)\) traveling-wave integral is satisfied by \(U_c\) for every test function \(\phi\) exactly when the endpoint coefficients
\[
A_1=bU^n,
\qquad A_2=b(U^n)',
\qquad A_3=-gU+aU^m+b(U^n)''
\]
vanish at \(\xi=\pm L\). For the weak \(KP(m,n)\) traveling-wave integral, the same conditions are required together with
\[
A_4=(-gU+aU^m)'+b(U^n)'''
\]
vanishing at \(\xi=\pm L\).

\section*{Premises}
\begin{align}
\text{(P1)}\quad &U_c(\xi)=U(\xi)H(L-|\xi|),
\qquad H(L-|\xi|)^q=H(L-|\xi|)\quad(q>0).\\
\text{(P2)}\quad &\int_{\mathbb R}\phi' fH\,d\xi
=\phi(L)f(L)-\phi(-L)f(-L)-\int_{\mathbb R}\phi f'H\,d\xi
\quad\text{for }f\in C^1.\\
\text{(P3)}\quad &I_K[U_c]:=\int_{\mathbb R}\left((-gU_c+aU_c^m)\phi'+bU_c^n\phi'''\right)d\xi.\\
\text{(P4)}\quad &I_{KP}[U_c]:=\int_{\mathbb R}\left((-gU_c+aU_c^m)\phi''+bU_c^n\phi''''\right)d\xi.\\
\text{(P5)}\quad &A_1:=bU^n,
\qquad A_2:=b(U^n)',
\qquad A_3:=-gU+aU^m+b(U^n)'',\\
& A_4:=(-gU+aU^m)'+b(U^n)'''.\\
\text{(P6)}\quad &\left(-gU+aU^m+b(U^n)''\right)'=0
\quad\text{on }[-L,L].\\
\text{(P7)}\quad &\left(-gU+aU^m+b(U^n)''\right)''=0
\quad\text{on }[-L,L].\\
\text{(P8)}\quad &\phi(\pm L),\ \phi'(\pm L),\ \phi''(\pm L),\ \phi'''(\pm L)
\text{ can be prescribed independently by test functions.}
\end{align}

\section*{Derivation}
For the \(K(m,n)\) weak integral, use (P1) in (P3):
\begin{align}
I_K[U_c]
&=\int_{\mathbb R}\left((-gU+aU^m)H\phi'+bU^nH\phi'''\right)d\xi
&&\text{by (P1)}.
\end{align}
Apply (P2) once to the first term and three times to the second term:
\begin{align}
I_K[U_c]
&=-\int_{\mathbb R}(-gU+aU^m)'H\phi\,d\xi
 -\int_{\mathbb R}b(U^n)'''H\phi\,d\xi
 -\left(\phi''A_1-\phi'A_2+\phi A_3\right)\Big|_{\xi=\pm L}\\
&=-\int_{\mathbb R}\left((-gU+aU^m)'+b(U^n)'''\right)H\phi\,d\xi
 -\left(\phi''A_1-\phi'A_2+\phi A_3\right)\Big|_{\xi=\pm L}.
\end{align}
Using (P6), the integral term vanishes:
\begin{align}
I_K[U_c]
&=-\left(\phi''A_1-\phi'A_2+\phi A_3\right)\Big|_{\xi=\pm L}.
\end{align}
By (P8), \(I_K[U_c]=0\) for all \(\phi\) exactly when
\begin{align}
A_1(\pm L)&=0,
& A_2(\pm L)&=0,
& A_3(\pm L)&=0.
\end{align}
For the \(KP(m,n)\) weak integral, use (P1) in (P4):
\begin{align}
I_{KP}[U_c]
&=\int_{\mathbb R}\left((-gU+aU^m)H\phi''+bU^nH\phi''''\right)d\xi.
\end{align}
Apply (P2) twice to the first term and four times to the second term:
\begin{align}
I_{KP}[U_c]
&=\int_{\mathbb R}\left((-gU+aU^m)''+b(U^n)''''\right)H\phi\,d\xi
 -\left(\phi'''A_1-\phi''A_2+\phi'A_3+\phi A_4\right)\Big|_{\xi=\pm L}.
\end{align}
Using (P7), the integral term vanishes:
\begin{align}
I_{KP}[U_c]
&=-\left(\phi'''A_1-\phi''A_2+\phi'A_3+\phi A_4\right)\Big|_{\xi=\pm L}.
\end{align}
By (P8), \(I_{KP}[U_c]=0\) for all \(\phi\) exactly when
\begin{align}
A_1(\pm L)&=0,
& A_2(\pm L)&=0,
& A_3(\pm L)&=0,
& A_4(\pm L)&=0.
\end{align}

\section*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{\begin{gathered}
K(m,n):\quad A_1(\pm L)=A_2(\pm L)=A_3(\pm L)=0,\\
KP(m,n):\quad A_1(\pm L)=A_2(\pm L)=A_3(\pm L)=A_4(\pm L)=0.
\end{gathered}}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_6:
\section*{Claim}
For a weak line compacton of the \(KP(m,n)\) equation, assume the \(K(m,n)\) cutoff condition \(pn>2\) already holds and impose the fourth endpoint condition \(A_4(\pm L)=0\). With the paper's endpoint expansion
\[
A_4\sim -gpU_0^p s^{p-1}+apmU_0^m s^{pm-1}+bpn(pn-1)(pn-2)U_0^n s^{pn-3},
\qquad s=L-|\xi|\to0^+,
\]
the paper's endpoint analysis gives the following six alternatives for \(A_4\to0\)
\[
\begin{gathered}
p>\max(1/m,3/n),\quad g=0,\\
p>\max(1/m,3/n),\quad m<1,\quad g\ne0,\\
p>\max(1,3/n),\quad m>1,\quad g\ne0,\\
1\ge p=\frac{2}{n-1},\quad 2m+1>n\ge3,\quad g\ne0,
\quad U_0=\left(\frac{g}{2b}\frac{(n-1)^2}{n(n+1)}\right)^{\frac{n-1}{(n-2)(n+1)}},\\
p=\frac{2}{n-m},\quad n\ge3m,\quad g=0,
\quad U_0=\left(-\frac{a}{2b}\frac{(n-m)^2}{n(n+m)}\right)^{\frac{1}{n-m}},\\
p=\frac{2}{n-m},\quad m+2>n\ge3m,\quad g\ne0,
\quad U_0=\left(-\frac{a}{2b}\frac{(n-m)^2}{n(n+m)}\right)^{\frac{1}{n-m}}.
\end{gathered}
\]

\section*{Premises}
\begin{align}
\text{(P1)}\quad &s:=L-|\xi|,
\qquad s\to0^+,
\qquad m,n,p>0,
\qquad m\ne1,
\qquad a,b\ne0,
\qquad U_0>0.\\
\text{(P2)}\quad &A_4\sim T_g+T_a+T_b,\\
\text{(P3)}\quad &T_g:=-gpU_0^p s^{p-1},
\qquad T_a:=apmU_0^m s^{pm-1},
\qquad T_b:=bpn(pn-1)(pn-2)U_0^n s^{pn-3}.\\
\text{(P4)}\quad &s^q\to0\text{ as }s\to0^+\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad q>0.\\
\text{(P5)}\quad &\text{Two nonzero leading powers }C_1s^r+C_2s^r\text{ cancel exactly when }C_1+C_2=0.\\
\text{(P6)}\quad &pn>2.
\end{align}

\section*{Derivation}
\textbf{Case 1: \(g=0\).} Then \(T_g=0\), so \(A_4\to0\) requires either separate decay of \(T_a,T_b\), or cancellation between their leading powers.
Separate decay gives
\begin{align}
pm-1&>0,
& pn-3&>0 &&\text{by (P3)--(P4)}\\
p&>\frac{1}{m},
& p&>\frac{3}{n} &&\text{because }m,n>0\\
p&>\max\left(\frac{1}{m},\frac{3}{n}\right).
\end{align}
For cancellation of \(T_a\) and \(T_b\), their exponents must agree and be nonpositive:
\begin{align}
pm-1&=pn-3\le0,\\
p(n-m)&=2,\\
p&=\frac{2}{n-m}. &&\text{since }p>0
\end{align}
The inequality \(pn-3\le0\) gives
\begin{align}
\frac{2n}{n-m}&\le3,\\
2n&\le3n-3m,\\
n&\ge3m.
\end{align}
The coefficient cancellation condition is
\begin{align}
apmU_0^m+bpn(pn-1)(pn-2)U_0^n&=0 &&\text{by (P3), (P5)}.
\end{align}
Substitute \(p=2/(n-m)\):
\begin{align}
a m+bn\left(\frac{n+m}{n-m}\right)\left(\frac{2m}{n-m}\right)U_0^{n-m}&=0 &&\text{divide by }pU_0^m,\\
a+\frac{2bn(n+m)}{(n-m)^2}U_0^{n-m}&=0 &&\text{divide by }m>0,\\
U_0&=\left(-\frac{a}{2b}\frac{(n-m)^2}{n(n+m)}\right)^{1/(n-m)}.
\end{align}
Thus \(g=0\) yields cases (35a) and (35e).

\textbf{Case 2: \(g\ne0\) and \(T_g\) cancels \(T_b\).} Since \(m\ne1\), \(T_g\) cannot cancel \(T_a\). Matching exponents of \(T_g\) and \(T_b\) gives
\begin{align}
p-1&=pn-3\le0,\\
p(n-1)&=2,\\
p&=\frac{2}{n-1},\\
1&\ge p,\qquad n\ge3.
\end{align}
The remaining term \(T_a\) must decay:
\begin{align}
pm-1&>0,\\
\frac{2m}{n-1}&>1,\\
2m+1&>n.
\end{align}
The coefficient cancellation condition is
\begin{align}
gU_0^p&=bn(pn-1)(pn-2)U_0^n &&\text{by (P3), (P5)}.
\end{align}
Substitute \(p=2/(n-1)\):
\begin{align}
U_0^{n-p}
&=\frac{g}{b n\left(\frac{n+1}{n-1}\right)\left(\frac{2}{n-1}\right)},\\
&=\frac{g}{2b}\frac{(n-1)^2}{n(n+1)},\\
n-p&=n-\frac{2}{n-1}=\frac{(n-2)(n+1)}{n-1},\\
U_0&=\left(\frac{g}{2b}\frac{(n-1)^2}{n(n+1)}\right)^{\frac{n-1}{(n-2)(n+1)}}.
\end{align}
This is case (35d).

\textbf{Case 3: \(g\ne0\) and \(T_g\) decays separately.} Then
\begin{align}
p-1&>0,\\
p&>1.
\end{align}
If \(m>1\), then \(pm>1\) follows from \(p>1\), so \(T_a\to0\). Requiring \(T_b\to0\) gives
\begin{align}
pn-3&>0,\\
p&>\frac{3}{n},\\
p&>\max\left(1,\frac{3}{n}\right),
\end{align}
which is case (35c).
If \(m<1\) and \(T_a,T_b\) decay separately, then
\begin{align}
pm-1&>0,
& pn-3&>0,\\
p&>\max\left(\frac{1}{m},\frac{3}{n}\right),
\end{align}
which is case (35b). If \(m<1\) and \(T_a,T_b\) cancel, the same calculation as in Case 1 gives
\begin{align}
p&=\frac{2}{n-m},
& n&\ge3m,
& U_0&=\left(-\frac{a}{2b}\frac{(n-m)^2}{n(n+m)}\right)^{1/(n-m)}.
\end{align}
The separate decay of \(T_g\) additionally gives
\begin{align}
p>1
&\Longleftrightarrow \frac{2}{n-m}>1,\\
&\Longleftrightarrow m+2>n.
\end{align}
This is case (35f). Finally, in cases (35a)--(35c), \(pn>3>2\). In case (35d), \(pn=2n/(n-1)>2\). In cases (35e)--(35f), \(pn=2n/(n-m)>2\). Thus (P6) is satisfied in all six cases.

\section*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{\begin{gathered}
(35a)\text{--}(35f)\text{ are exactly the endpoint alternatives for }A_4(\pm L)=0,\\
\text{and each alternative implies }pn>2.
\end{gathered}}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_7:
\section*{Claim}
For a compacton profile with endpoint behavior
\[
U(\xi)\sim U_0(L-|\xi|)^p,
\qquad U_0\ne0,
\]
the endpoint differentiability condition for a strong \(K(m,n)\) compacton is equivalent to
\[
p>3.
\]
The endpoint differentiability condition for a strong \(KP(m,n)\) line compacton is equivalent to
\[
p>4.
\]

\section*{Premises}
\begin{align}
\text{(P1)}\quad &s:=L-|\xi|,
\qquad s\to0^+,
\qquad U(\xi)\sim U_0s^p,
\qquad U_0\ne0.\\
\text{(P2)}\quad &\frac{d^j}{d\xi^j}(L\mp\xi)^p
=(\mp1)^j p(p-1)\cdots(p-j+1)(L\mp\xi)^{p-j}.\\
\text{(P3)}\quad &s^q\to0\text{ as }s\to0^+\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad q>0.\\
\text{(P4)}\quad &\text{A strong }K(m,n)\text{ compacton requires }U,U',U'',U'''
\text{ to vanish at }\xi=\pm L.\\
\text{(P5)}\quad &\text{A strong }KP(m,n)\text{ line compacton requires }U,U',U'',U''',U''''
\text{ to vanish at }\xi=\pm L.
\end{align}

\section*{Derivation}
For derivative order \(j\), (P1)--(P2) imply
\begin{align}
U^{(j)}(\xi)&\sim C_j s^{p-j},
\end{align}
where \(C_j\) is the corresponding nonzero leading coefficient when no endpoint cancellation is imposed. By (P3),
\begin{align}
U^{(j)}(\xi)\to0
&\Longleftrightarrow p-j>0,\\
&\Longleftrightarrow p>j.
\end{align}
For the \(K(m,n)\) equation, (P4) requires this for \(j=0,1,2,3\). Hence
\begin{align}
U,U',U'',U'''\to0
&\Longleftrightarrow p>0,
\quad p>1,
\quad p>2,
\quad p>3,\\
&\Longleftrightarrow p>3.
\end{align}
For the \(KP(m,n)\) equation, (P5) requires this for \(j=0,1,2,3,4\). Hence
\begin{align}
U,U',U'',U''',U''''\to0
&\Longleftrightarrow p>0,
\quad p>1,
\quad p>2,
\quad p>3,
\quad p>4,\\
&\Longleftrightarrow p>4.
\end{align}

\section*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{\text{strong }K(m,n):\ p>3,\qquad \text{strong }KP(m,n):\ p>4.}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_8:
\section*{Claim}
For \(n>1\), \(m=n\), and \(\operatorname{sgn}(g)=\operatorname{sgn}(a)=\operatorname{sgn}(b)\), define
\[
r:=\frac{2}{n-1},
\qquad
K:=\left(\frac{2ng}{(n+1)a}\right)^{1/(n-1)},
\qquad
\lambda:=\frac{n-1}{2n}\sqrt{\frac{a}{b}},
\qquad
L:=\frac{\pi}{2\lambda}.
\]
Then the cosine profile
\[
U(\xi):=K\cos(\lambda\xi)^r,
\qquad |\xi|<L,
\]
satisfies the traveling-wave ODE
\[
\left(-gU+aU^n+b(U^n)''\right)'=0,
\]
and its cutoff
\[
U_c(\xi):=U(\xi)H(L-|\xi|)
\]
is a weak \(K(n,n)\) compacton with endpoint exponent \(p=2/(n-1)>2/n\).

\section*{Premises}
\begin{align}
\text{(P1)}\quad &n>1,
\qquad m=n,
\qquad a,b,g\ne0,
\qquad \operatorname{sgn}(g)=\operatorname{sgn}(a)=\operatorname{sgn}(b).\\
\text{(P2)}\quad &r:=\frac{2}{n-1},
\qquad q:=rn=\frac{2n}{n-1}=r+2.\\
\text{(P3)}\quad &K:=\left(\frac{2ng}{(n+1)a}\right)^{1/(n-1)},
\qquad
\lambda:=\frac{n-1}{2n}\sqrt{\frac{a}{b}},
\qquad L:=\frac{\pi}{2\lambda}.\\
\text{(P4)}\quad &C(\xi):=\cos(\lambda\xi),
\qquad S(\xi):=\sin(\lambda\xi),
\qquad S^2=1-C^2.\\
\text{(P5)}\quad &C'=-\lambda S,
\qquad S'=\lambda C.\\
\text{(P6)}\quad &U(\xi):=KC^r,
\qquad |\xi|<L.\\
\text{(P7)}\quad &A_1:=bU^n,
\qquad A_2:=b(U^n)',
\qquad A_3:=-gU+aU^n+b(U^n)''.\\
\text{(P8)}\quad &\text{If }U\text{ satisfies }(-gU+aU^n+b(U^n)'')'=0\text{ on }[-L,L]
\text{ and }A_1(\pm L)=A_2(\pm L)=A_3(\pm L)=0,\\
&\text{then }U_c(\xi)=U(\xi)H(L-|\xi|)\text{ satisfies the weak }K(n,n)\text{ traveling-wave integral.}\\
\text{(P9)}\quad &s^\alpha\to0\text{ as }s\to0^+\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \alpha>0.
\end{align}

\section*{Derivation}
First compute the second derivative of \(C^q\):
\begin{align}
(C^q)'
&=qC^{q-1}C' &&\text{by the chain rule}\\
&=-q\lambda C^{q-1}S &&\text{by (P5)},\\
(C^q)''
&=-q\lambda\left((q-1)C^{q-2}C'S+C^{q-1}S'\right) &&\text{differentiate}\\
&=-q\lambda\left((q-1)C^{q-2}(-\lambda S)S+C^{q-1}(\lambda C)\right) &&\text{by (P5)}\\
&=q(q-1)\lambda^2C^{q-2}S^2-q\lambda^2C^q\\
&=q(q-1)\lambda^2C^{q-2}(1-C^2)-q\lambda^2C^q &&\text{by (P4)}\\
&=q(q-1)\lambda^2C^{q-2}-q^2\lambda^2C^q.
\end{align}
Using \(q=r+2\), (P6), and \(m=n\), obtain
\begin{align}
U^n&=K^nC^q,\\
(U^n)''&=K^nq(q-1)\lambda^2C^r-K^nq^2\lambda^2C^{r+2}.
\end{align}
Hence
\begin{align}
-gU+aU^n+b(U^n)''
&=-gKC^r+aK^nC^{r+2}
+bK^nq(q-1)\lambda^2C^r-bK^nq^2\lambda^2C^{r+2}\\
&=\left(-gK+bK^nq(q-1)\lambda^2\right)C^r
+\left(aK^n-bK^nq^2\lambda^2\right)C^{r+2}.
\end{align}
The coefficient of \(C^{r+2}\) is zero because
\begin{align}
q^2\lambda^2
&=\left(\frac{2n}{n-1}\right)^2
\left(\frac{n-1}{2n}\right)^2\frac{a}{b} &&\text{by (P2)--(P3)}\\
&=\frac{a}{b},\\
aK^n-bK^nq^2\lambda^2&=aK^n-bK^n\frac{a}{b}=0.
\end{align}
The coefficient of \(C^r\) is zero because
\begin{align}
q(q-1)\lambda^2
&=\frac{2n}{n-1}\frac{n+1}{n-1}
\left(\frac{n-1}{2n}\right)^2\frac{a}{b} &&\text{by (P2)--(P3)}\\
&=\frac{a(n+1)}{2nb},\\
-gK+bK^nq(q-1)\lambda^2
&=K\left(-g+K^{n-1}\frac{a(n+1)}{2n}\right)\\
&=K\left(-g+\frac{2ng}{(n+1)a}\frac{a(n+1)}{2n}\right) &&\text{by (P3)}\\
&=0.
\end{align}
Therefore
\begin{align}
-gU+aU^n+b(U^n)''&=0,\\
\left(-gU+aU^n+b(U^n)''\right)'&=0.
\end{align}
It remains to check the cutoff endpoint coefficients in (P7). Since \(\lambda L=\pi/2\),
\begin{align}
C(L)&=\cos(\pi/2)=0,
& C(-L)&=\cos(-\pi/2)=0.
\end{align}
Near \(\xi=L\), \(C'(L)=-\lambda\), and near \(\xi=-L\), \(C'(-L)=\lambda\). Hence
\begin{align}
C(\xi)&\sim \lambda(L-|\xi|),\\
U(\xi)&=KC^r\sim K\lambda^r(L-|\xi|)^r.
\end{align}
Thus the endpoint exponent is
\begin{align}
p&=r=\frac{2}{n-1}.
\end{align}
Moreover
\begin{align}
U^n&\sim K^n\lambda^q(L-|\xi|)^q,\\
(U^n)'&\sim \pm qK^n\lambda^q(L-|\xi|)^{q-1},\\
q&=\frac{2n}{n-1}>2 &&\text{because }n>1.
\end{align}
By (P7)--(P9),
\begin{align}
A_1(\pm L)&=0,\\
A_2(\pm L)&=0,\\
A_3(\pm L)&=0 &&\text{because }-gU+aU^n+b(U^n)''=0\text{ on }(-L,L).
\end{align}
Therefore (P8) implies that \(U_c=UH(L-|\xi|)\) is a weak \(K(n,n)\) compacton. Finally,
\begin{align}
p-\frac{2}{n}
&=\frac{2}{n-1}-\frac{2}{n}\\
&=\frac{2}{n(n-1)}>0 &&\text{because }n>1,
\end{align}
so \(p>2/n\), and
\begin{align}
L=\frac{\pi}{2\lambda}
&=\frac{\pi}{2}\frac{2n}{n-1}\sqrt{\frac{b}{a}}\\
&=\frac{n}{n-1}\sqrt{\frac{b}{a}}\,\pi.
\end{align}

\section*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{U_c(\xi)=\left(\frac{2ng}{(n+1)a}\right)^{1/(n-1)}
\cos\left(\frac{n-1}{2n}\sqrt{\frac{a}{b}}\,\xi\right)^{2/(n-1)}H(L-|\xi|),
\quad L=\frac{n}{n-1}\sqrt{\frac{b}{a}}\,\pi,
\quad p=\frac{2}{n-1}>\frac{2}{n}.}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
